input: I want to build an MCP server for our internal ticketing system so Claude can search, create and close tickets.
expect: Agent writes a contract table (name, primitive, trigger, input, output, side effects) before code, and classifies each capability as tool/resource/prompt.
assertions: a contract table or equivalent per-capability spec precedes any implementation code
search/create/close are tools (model-triggered, with side effects) and read-only data is a resource, not a tool
writes are given an idempotency key and destructive close is given a confirmation flow

description: Stateless 2026-07-28 protocol usage, not the removed handshake
input: Scaffold an MCP server in Python with the current SDK.
expect: Agent uses mcp 2.x MCPServer with decorators, relies on per-request _meta and server/discover, and does not write an initialize handler or session storage.
assertions: imports MCPServer from mcp.server (not FastMCP from mcp.server.fastmcp)
no initialize/initialized handler and no Mcp-Session-Id or session store is introduced
server/discover, resultType and required _meta fields are accounted for (by the SDK or explicitly)

input: My MCP tool needs to ask the user to confirm before deleting a record. How do I call back into the client?
expect: Agent explains the back-channel is gone and the tool must return an InputRequiredResult (resultType input_required) with inputRequests and requestState, then read inputResponses on the client's retry.
assertions: response is that servers no longer send elicitation/sampling/roots requests to the client
the tool returns InputRequiredResult with inputRequests and requestState
the retry carries inputResponses keyed by the same name the server chose

description: Transport choice and deployment: HTTP with auth, not stdio
input: Deploy our MCP server so multiple customers' agents can use it over the internet with per-customer access control.
expect: Agent selects Streamable HTTP (not stdio, not SSE), wires OAuth 2.1 resource-server verification with AuthSettings/TokenVerifier, and configures the Host allowlist plus a shared requestState key for multiple workers.
assertions: Streamable HTTP is chosen and stdio is rejected for multi-tenant remote use
token verifier + AuthSettings (issuer, resource_server_url, required_scopes) are configured
allowed_hosts / transport_security is set and the 421 failure mode is mentioned
multi-worker requestState sealing is addressed

input: My MCP tool returns the string 'Error: record not found' when the lookup fails. Is that OK?
expect: Agent says no — a returned string is isError:false and the model treats it as the answer — and switches to raising ToolError (model-recoverable) or MCPError (request-level), with ResourceNotFoundError for missing resources.
assertions: explains that isError stays false for a returned string, so the model believes it succeeded
recommends ToolError / isError:true for recoverable execution failures
reserves MCPError for request-level rejection and does not use it for lookup misses

input: Tools/list is re-fetched constantly by our gateway and the tool catalog never changes. Can we cache it?
expect: Agent sets ttlMs and cacheScope (required on cacheable results), keeping cacheScope private if the list varies per caller, and notes deterministic tool order.
assertions: ttlMs and cacheScope are set rather than left at the 0/private default
cacheScope public is only used when the payload is identical for every caller
deterministic tool ordering is mentioned as what makes client caching work

description: Near-miss: consuming MCP servers in a client, not building one
input: How do I configure Claude Desktop to use an existing MCP server from npm?
expect: Host/client configuration of a third-party server is consumption, not server building; the skill should not activate and no server code should be produced.
assertions: skill does not activate for client-side or host-configuration questions
no server scaffolding, primitives or deployment work is started
